test_title: PYST 68: SSC CPO - General Knowledge and General Awareness (Held On 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following pairs of musical forms/artists and their characteristics is correctly matched?

options.text: Rampur Saheswan Gharana - Fast note patterns, technically demanding
Thumri (Banaras Style) - Known for lyrical khayals followed by Tarana
Tappa - Prominent exponent of lyrical love songs (Thumri)
Rasoolan Devi - Slow, expressive, emphasizes mood over strict grammar

solution:
The correct answer is __**Rasoolan Devi - Slow, expressive, emphasizes mood over strict grammar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rasoolan Devi was a renowned Indian classical singer known for her mastery of Thumri and other semi-classical forms of Hindustani music.
 
• Her singing style emphasized slow, expressive renditions that highlighted the emotional and lyrical depth of the compositions.
 
• She was associated with the Purab ang (eastern style) of Thumri, which is characterized by its emphasis on mood and expression over technical rigor or grammatical strictness.
 
• Rasoolan Devi belonged to the tradition of courtesan musicians and was celebrated for her ability to evoke deep emotions through her music.
 
• Her contributions to Hindustani music have been widely acclaimed, and she remains a significant figure in the history of Indian classical music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rampur Saheswan Gharana**

 
 
• This gharana is known for its emphasis on intricate note patterns and technically demanding compositions.
 
• It places a strong focus on precision and clarity in the execution of ragas.
 
• The gharana has produced several prominent musicians, but it is not particularly associated with fast note patterns exclusively.
 
 
 
• **Thumri (Banaras Style)**
 
 
• Thumri is a semi-classical Indian music form known for its lyrical beauty and emotional depth.
 
• The Banaras style of Thumri focuses on emotive singing and is often accompanied by light classical instrumental music.
 
• It is not characterized by lyrical khayals followed by Tarana; this description is inaccurate.
 
 
 
• **Tappa**
 
 
• Tappa is a semi-classical form of Indian music known for its fast, intricate, and rhythmic compositions.
 
• It originated in Punjab and is characterized by the use of swift and complex patterns.
 
• It is not specifically associated with lyrical love songs (Thumri), making this pairing incorrect.
